controls: Limit the change to the eltwise/activation vector-math emitter path; leave other JIT paths untouched until A/B confirms no regression.
Verify the materialized registers are properly marked live-in/live-across so the emitter's register allocator does not introduce spills (currently none are visible).
A/B with benchdnn on the eltwise_f16 upstream testcase; roll back if avg_ms regresses on small tensors (benchdnn_min_ms 0.172 ms is the small-tensor floor).
reasons: Hoisting constants lengthens live ranges across the whole loop and could increase register pressure in the emitter's allocation model.
The change touches shared JIT code paths that also generate other eltwise variants (sigmoid/softplus/tanh/exp), risking collateral changes in kernel size and behavior.
If the JIT emits straight-line code without an explicit loop-invariant analysis, the hoist must be gated by a real CFG-level proof or it could be applied where the backedge does not exist.

conditions.description: Coefficients are compile-time constants per generated kernel (the annotate shows the same lui+addiw+fmv.w.x sites every iteration with identical immediates 0xc2aebac0, 0x42b17218, 0x3fb8aa3b, 0x3f000000, 0x3f800000, 0x40000000, etc.).
Materialization target registers are dead before the loop body or only reused across iterations, and no CFG branch or exception edge between backedge and body modifies them.
The JIT emitter recognizes the fixed-VL main loop structure (backedge at 0x1d4) so hoisting is legal and reachable.
oneDNN eltwise reference accepts the unchanged coefficient values (bit-identical constants, so no rounding/ULP change).

actions.proposal: In oneDNN's RISC-V CPU JIT emitter, make the elementwise-activation generator recognize the vector-math FP coefficients as loop-invariant and hoist their lui+addiw+fmv.w.x materialization out of the fixed-VL main loop (materialize once before the loop into FP/vector registers that are live across the backedge), instead of re-emitting the ~15 constant sites on every iteration.

correctness_checks: Run benchdnn eltwise_f16 functional validation and compare outputs with the scalar/reference path before and after the emitter change.
Verify NaN, +/-Inf, +/-0, subnormal, and FRM/FCSR behavior is unchanged by the hoisted materialization.
Confirm hoisted constants are bit-identical to the in-loop values by dumping the emitted kernel and comparing immediate fields.

expected_signals.signal: The ~15 per-iteration lui/addiw/fmv.w.x materialization sites (0xa0, 0xb4, 0xc4, 0xdc, 0x100, 0x108, 0x124, 0x138, 0x14c, 0x160, 0x174, 0x18c, 0x1ac) no longer appear inside the annotated loop interval 0x8c..0x1d4; their combined ~58% hotspot share drops to near zero.
Dynamic instruction count per eltwise_f16 iteration falls (perf stat instructions and benchdnn avg_ms decrease); IPC (currently 0.679) rises toward the kernel's vector-FMA bound.
One loop-invariant FP-constant setup sequence appears before the loop entry (0x8c), executed once instead of per iteration.
eltwise_f16 numerical results and special-value behavior stay identical; no new branch-miss or cache-miss increase appears (branch_miss_rate currently 0.360%, L1 miss 0.328%).

success_criteria: Emitted eltwise_f16 loop body contains zero per-iteration lui/addiw/fmv.w.x constant-materialization sequences; constants are set up once before 0x8c.
benchdnn eltwise_f16_upstream avg_ms decreases relative to the 0.184253 ms baseline with no functional mismatch.

controls: Reuse vector state only when the emitter can prove single-predecessor backedge with no clobbering call/asm/exception edge; otherwise keep the current invalidation.
Verify with annotated output after regeneration that exactly one setup remains before the loop and none inside the interval.
Gate the change behind the fixed-VL main-loop shape so runtime-VL tail loops (which legitimately re-run vsetvl) are unaffected.
reasons: Reusing vector state across a label/join without a CFG meet is the classic correctness failure of this pattern; the emitter's exact invalidation point is not directly visible in annotate (Medium route confidence).
The single vsetvli is a small per-iteration cost, so the benefit is limited and must not be oversold; combined with the root-cause change it compounds.
An exception or context-restore boundary between iterations would make the state incompatible; the emitter must not skip setup then.

conditions.description: The loop is a fixed-VL main loop: vl and vtype are identical every iteration (backedge 0x1d4 -> 0x8c re-executes the vsetvli-style setup at 0x9c).
No call, inline assembly, or faulting-vector-state boundary intervenes between the backedge and the vsetvli, so compatible state can be proven.
The emitter maintains vector-state (vl/vtype) knowledge across branch emission and can skip redundant setup.

actions.proposal: Make the oneDNN RISC-V JIT emitter's vector-state tracking survive loop backedge emission for fixed-VL main loops: emit vsetvli once before the loop when vl/vtype are proven compatible, and skip the redundant per-iteration setup (0x9c) rather than invalidating state at every branch/label (the rvv_vector_state_management invalidation-point rule).

correctness_checks: Benchdnn eltwise_f16 functional tests across sizes that are and are not multiples of VLEN/4 lanes to confirm tails remain correct.
Verify vtype policy and vl semantics are unchanged by inspecting the emitted kernel before and after; no illegal-vtype or tail-fragment regression.
Test exception/fault paths that could invalidate vector state (per rvv_vector_state_management boundaries) remain correctly handled.

expected_signals.signal: The vsetvli-style setup at 0x9c disappears from the annotated loop interval 0x8c..0x1d4 in the regenerated kernel.
Per-iteration instruction count and total function instructions (perf stat instruction) drop slightly; hotspot share at loop-control lines falls.
A single vsetvli appears before the loop entry and is not re-executed on the backedge.
Vector output and tail behavior remain bit-identical; no new vsetvl appears after a call or label join in the emitted CFG.

success_criteria: The regenerated kernel's loop interval contains no vsetvli; exactly one compatible setup precedes the loop.
benchdnn eltwise_f16 output matches reference exactly and avg_ms does not regress; ideally a small additional decrease over the root-cause change alone.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Constant-pool/code-layout frontend pressure: the loop is only ~0xd8 bytes and perf stat shows no meaningful i-cache signal (cache_references 3.97M vs 42.5T instructions is a scaling artifact; no frontend-stall counter available), so frontend footprint is not the demonstrated bottleneck; the row requires frontend/i-cache evidence to own the finding.

Dependency-chain/scheduling latency: the lui->addiw->fmv.w.x->vf*.vv chain feeds the FMA recurrence, so some low-IPC cost may be latency rather than pure issue. On the OoO C920v2 this is secondary; removing the redundant instructions removes both issue and dependency cost.

findings.conclusion: The oneDNN RISC-V JIT emitter rematerializes the same set of ~15 single-precision activation coefficients inside the hot eltwise_f16 loop body on every iteration instead of hoisting them out of the loop, adding ~30 scalar lui/addiw/fmv.w.x instructions per iteration that dominate the hot interval (lui hotspots at 0x18c 9.68%, 0xa0/0xc4/0x138/0x160/0x174/0x1ac 6.45% each, plus ~15 lines at 3.23%); the loop is compute/issue-bound, not memory- or branch-bound (L1 miss 0.328%, branch miss 0.360%, IPC 0.679).

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Row requires frontend/i-cache evidence (pool-skipping jumps, I-cache misses, frontend stalls); perf stat exposes no such counter and the loop footprint is ~0xd8 bytes, so constant-pool layout is not the demonstrated bottleneck.

Row requires a missing/incorrect target-core latency/resource model plus PMU/dependency evidence; no scheduler dump or C920v2 stall counters are available, and the redundancy is structural (extra instructions), not ordering.
Row covers rounding/NaN/boxing/FCSR semantic preservation; the constants here are arithmetic coefficients materialized for FMA operands, not FP-semantic guard sequences.
Row is scoped to integer/address constant construction (lui/addi/slli); these are single-precision FP values moved via fmv.w.x for vector FMA operands.

findings.reasoning: Provenance is directly JIT-generated code (jit_uni_kernel.0 in jitted-12109-0.so). Annotate shows 15 lui+addiw+fmv.w.x constant-materialization sites whose aggregate sample share is ~58% of the function's hotspot samples, all inside the single loop interval (0x8c backedge 0x1d4). The coefficients (0x3f800000, 0x3f000000, 0x40000000, 0x42b17218, 0xc2aeac50, 0x3fb8aa3b, 0x3f318... through 0x3e2aaaaa) are loop-invariant FP polynomial/FMA coefficients for a softplus/exp-family activation and never change across iterations. The emitter fails to recognize them as loop-invariant (JIT-quality 'redundant constant loads in generated sequences'). Bound type: instructions-per-cycle 0.679 with near-zero cache and branch miss rates indicates issue-bandwidth/dependency-bound execution where removing scalar materialization directly lowers dynamic instruction count.

alternative_explanations.explanation: A runtime-VL tail loop legitimately re-running vsetvl each iteration would not be redundant; here the kernel uses a fixed-step main loop with no runtime-VL tail in the annotated body, and the branch count (269.9M total, 0.360% miss) is consistent with a single simple backedge, weakening but not fully refuting this at Medium confidence.

This is the same emitter-quality mechanism as the root cause (redundant emission inside the loop), so as an independent root cause it is weakened; it is best treated as a supporting sub-signal of the JIT-quality finding.

findings.conclusion: The JIT-emitted loop re-executes the vsetvli-style vector-state setup at 0x9c on every iteration (backedge 0x1d4 -> 0x8c) even though vl and vtype are loop-invariant with no intervening call, inline asm, or state clobber, adding a redundant vector-configuration instruction to the fixed-VL main loop body.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The finding is repeated compatible vector-state setup inside the loop, not LMUL/register-group sizing; only one vsetvli per iteration exists, so this is not an LMUL-underutilization mechanism.
The scalar FP constants feed a long vfwmacc/vfmadd chain and are not single-consumer splat broadcasts, so the vx/vi form row does not own the materialization.

findings.reasoning: The function is a fixed-VL main loop: pointer advances by slli t1,t0,1 (element*2), a4-=t0, unconditional backedge j 0x8c; the vsetvli-style instruction at 0x9c (encoding 0x0d12f057, vsetvli rd,rs1,vtype class) re-executes each iteration with no state-modifying instruction in between. rvv_vector_state_management's profile signal is 'repeated vsetvli in a hot vector loop with no intervening instruction that changes vl/vtype', met here; route confidence Medium because the emitter's invalidation point is inferred from the emitted loop rather than direct emitter source, and the instruction is a single per-iteration cost subsumed by the JIT-quality root cause.

alternative_explanations.explanation: If a source-level RVV exp/tanh approximation is available but the emitted polynomial coefficients were being recomputed per element rather than per iteration, the activation pipeline could still be tuned; however, the observed problem is loop-invariant materialization inside the loop, which is a JIT-quality mechanism, not the activation algorithm.

findings.conclusion: The rvv_elementwise_activation_kernels pattern does not match this hotspot: the eltwise_f16 softplus/exp activation is already fully RVV-vectorized with no scalar branches/selects, parameter broadcasts, math-helper calls, or range reduction dominating; the hot samples are in already-vectorized vfwmacc/vfmadd/vse-style code and the scalar lui materialization, not in an unvectorized activation path.
findings.reasoning: The row's positive signals (scalar branch/select or exp/tanh helper dominating) are absent: the annotated loop body is an RVV FMA chain (encodings 0xe0..0x1b8 are vfwmacc/vfmadd/vse family) with the only scalar overhead being coefficient materialization, which belongs to the JIT-quality finding. The kernel is already the vector-math form the pattern would prescribe; no unvectorized activation body exists to fix.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The f16->f32 widening is an inherent input stage; if its SEW/LMUL choice were mismatched it could add vsetvli churn, but only one vector-state setup per iteration is observed, so conversion configuration is not the demonstrated cost.

findings.conclusion: The rvv_precision_conversion_kernels pattern does not match: the f16->f32 widening for eltwise_f16 is already performed with RVV widening instructions (vfwmacc/vfwadd-style encodings at 0xe0/0xe4 and halfword-scaled loads at 0x90), with no scalar conversion helper, per-element special-value branching, or pack/unpack emulation dominating samples; conversion is a sub-step of an activation whose samples are dominated by the FMA chain and constant materialization.
findings.reasoning: The row applies only when conversion work itself dominates samples; here no conversion instruction or helper address shows a meaningful share, the pattern explicitly states that when an activation dominates, the operator pattern owns it, and the conversion is already a vector widening with correct vtype setup. No conversion-specific hotspot exists to repair.

operator_rvv.reason: The kernel is an already-vectorized elementwise activation (eltwise_f16_upstream): vle16/vle32-style f16 load, f32 widening multiply/FMA chain with exp/sigmoid polynomial constants, and vector store. from-profile Step 0d requires rows-operator-rvv.md when independent evidence points to an operator algorithm; the elementwise-activation semantic row and widening/precision behavior are relevant to the compute body even though code is already vectorized.

runtime_os.reason: No timer, interrupt, privileged-boundary, CSR-context, or runtime-context-management signal. perf stat branch_miss_rate 0.360% and the annotate body show a plain compute loop with one branch (beqz 0x8c) and one backedge; no sync, spin, or privilege activity.

string_memory.reason: Workload is numeric elementwise activation on contiguous f16 buffers, not string/memory/compare/checksum/copy/fill work. No mem*/str* helper, IFUNC resolver, or word-alignment/sentinel/back-reference evidence in annotate or perf stat (L1 miss rate 0.328%).

vectorized_tuning.reason: Annotate already contains RVV 1.0 v* instructions (vsetvli at 0x9c, vfwmacc/vfwnmacc/vfmacc-family .insn at 0xe0..0x1b8) in a JIT-generated (non-.S) kernel, hardware RVV 1.0 with VLEN=128 (vlenb=16) on C920v2. Per-iteration vector-state setup and fixed-VL main-loop overhead are within rows-vectorized-tuning.md (rvv_vector_state_management row belongs to rows-codegen.md per class index; rows-vectorized-tuning covers configuration/register/unroll/operand/inactive-lane rows).

summary.observed_anomaly: The oneDNN RISC-V JIT emitter rematerializes the same set of ~15 single-precision activation coefficients inside the hot eltwise_f16 loop body on every iteration instead of hoisting them out of the loop, adding ~30 scalar lui/addiw/fmv.w.x instructions per iteration that dominate the hot interval (lui hotspots at 0x18c 9.68%, 0xa0/0xc4/0x138/0x160/0x174/0x1ac 6.45% each, plus ~15 lines at 3.23%); the loop is compute/issue-bound, not memory- or branch-bound (L1 miss 0.328%, branch miss 0.360%, IPC 0.679).
